rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent mass in all four views and the non-rectangular footprint is real, but the dominant figure remains a mostly sealed bar/block with only a modest west-side notch. The blue access edge is acknowledged, yet the response is semantically weak: no strong public court, undercut, or entry seam opens toward it, so the active-ground requirement is only partially met. The top and isometric views show some plan complexity and a carved edge, but the section is flat and generic rather than expressing a clear public void/terrace hierarchy. It is not visibly self-contradictory, so repair integrity is good, but program fit fails the hard pass because neighborhood living here needs a more legible street threshold and more explicit public/open-space logic.
